hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of x squared and a length of three x.  At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative five x and the length is three x. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of six with a length of three x.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{3x}(x^2-5x+6)
\\\\
&=\goldE{3x}(x^2)+\goldE{3x}(-5x)+\goldE{3x}(6)
\\\\
&=3x^3-15x^2+18x
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of x squared and a length of three x. Inside of this rectangle is three x cubed. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative five x and the length is three x. Inside of this rectangle is negative fifteen x squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of six with a length of three x. Inside of this rectangle is eighteen x.
